metadata.title: Inside Tesla’s Cybertruck and robotaxi experience

content.text:
A week after Tesla's (TSLA) Cybertruck launch, The Verge Freelance Reporter Mack DeGeurin joins Ines Ferre on Market Domination to break down how the Cybertruck works and take viewers inside Tesla's highly anticipated robotaxi experience.
Mac, you wrote about this uh experience on the Verge. Tell us about this ride in the cyber cab. How was it?
Yeah, it was interesting. I mean, I've been covering robotaxis for quite a while now and so this is really, you know, Tesla's big shot at entering the market in a big way. So I was pretty curious to see what it was like.
Um, you know, I think in my story, the way I described it was equal parts nerve-wracking and boring. Um, and boring in this case is uh a good thing. You know, when you have one of these vehicles that's supposed to be driving itself, the last thing you want is some unexpected experience, something that makes you nervous.
Um, and for the most part, the ride was to be expected. You know, it took you where you needed to go, albeit the wait times were quite long. Um, and um it worked largely as intended. That said, there's were some issues as well. Um, you know, there's some growing pains.
When I was let off of the vehicle, uh sometimes it would pick up or drop people off kind of in the middle of a road, um which would temporarily build up traffic. Um there's also instances where I'd be kind of going in one direction and the car would change lanes for no apparent reason, always getting you where it needed to go, but um it just felt a little bit unconfident for something that doesn't have steering wheels or pedals or any of the normal things you expect from a car.
So, um, it was a mixed bag, I would say.
And and how was it being in a car without steering or a steering wheel, without pedals? And can you talk to it? I mean, does it have sort of a voice recognition so you can say, hey, slow down or there's a person right there, don't crash. I mean, is there a way for you to be able to command this car?
So, I mean, in short, no. The way it all works is that you download Tesla's robotaxi app and that's how you summon it kind of like you would with an Uber. And once you're in, you have your destination there and it takes control. You know, you don't see a steering wheel, you don't see any pedals.
Um, and you do have on this big touchscreen that's in the center, um, a map that shows where you're going and it shows a digital representation of pedestrians of other cars. But in terms of your actual control, it's, you know, you're giving it up to the to the vehicle. and that's the same with Waymo and other robotaxis as well.
Um, there is um a stop button, so you can have it pull over if you want. Um, and you can also communicate with a human operator by pressing a button. Um,
and they also have, which I didn't really test too much, but Grock, uh uh XAI's, you know, AI chatbot, you can interact with that in the vehicle too, but that doesn't change the way the vehicle works. It's mostly just, you know, getting information the way you would with another chatbot.
And how does it compare to Tesla's Model Y Robo taxi?
Yeah, I mean, it's interesting because so the the Model Y released here in Austin as well, um around June last year. Um and the software that's underpinning both of them is very similar, but the experience is really different because the the Model Y, it's kind of like a Waymo, it's a retrofitted car. So you have a steering wheel, you have pedals. This is a lot different because this is kind of the glimpses to the future where it's a purpose built vehicle meant specifically for autonomy.
Um, you know, just in my personal experience, this feels a lot more with the cyber cab kind of like the thing that you're promised, right? It's a Musk has described it as a lounge on wheels. Um, and to an extent it feels like that, right?
You're secluded, it's just a two-seater, you're in there either on the driver seat or the passenger seat with view, a big screen, um, and you know, surround sound audio. Um so it's a much more, I would say like immersive future forward feeling experience than in the Model Y version.
